classes.name: Methylphenidate stimulants
classes.description: CNS stimulants in the methylphenidate family: methylphenidate IR/ER (Ritalin, Concerta, Metadate, Aptensio, Jornay PM, Quillichew, Cotempla), dexmethylphenidate IR/ER (Focalin), serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate (Azstarys), methylphenidate patch (Daytrana).
classes.plainDescription: A stimulant pill or patch for ADHD from the Ritalin/Concerta family.

classes.name: Amphetamine stimulants
classes.description: CNS stimulants in the amphetamine family: mixed amphetamine salts IR/ER (Adderall, Adderall XR, Mydayis), lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse, capsule and chewable), dextroamphetamine (Dexedrine, Zenzedi, Xelstrym patch), amphetamine sulfate (Evekeo), amphetamine ER (Adzenys, Dyanavel).
classes.plainDescription: A stimulant for ADHD from the Adderall/Vyvanse family.

classes.name: Non-stimulant ADHD agents
classes.description: Non-stimulant ADHD agents: atomoxetine (Strattera), viloxazine ER (Qelbree), guanfacine ER (Intuniv), clonidine ER (Kapvay).
classes.plainDescription: A daily ADHD medicine that is not a stimulant.

records.verificationNote: Read FL Medicaid PDL effective 10/01/2026, pp.32-33 (flat table; PA Required column). Preferred pick: generic IR methylphenidate 10 mg, PA column No, age 0+ (judgment: cheapest and most commonly prescribed MPH with no PA). Concerta brand and generic ER are both PA column No, so no brand-over-generic preference is stated (boglActive false). Jornay PM is Auto PA. Ritalin, Quillichew, Cotempla and Azstarys do not appear in the PDL and are recorded as PA required (not on the PDL) per the brief convention. Sig is standard label dosing; not stated in the PDL. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: removed 4 absence-only PA/nonformulary entries (Ritalin (methylphenidate brand), Quillichew ER (methylphenidate chewable), Cotempla XR-ODT (methylphenidate), Azstarys (serdexmethylphenidate/dexmethylphenidate)): the PDL (pp.1-2 definitions) says nothing about non-listed drugs requiring PA, so absence is not evidence]

records.verificationNote: Read from the PDL text layer, pp.22-23 (section 'Central Nervous System Agents - Drugs for Attention Deficit Disorder'). Legend p.5: E = may be excluded from coverage or subject to PA in CT, NJ and NY; ST = step therapy; QL = quantity limit. E-flagged brands are recorded as outcome 'pa' because the legend names PA as the NY mechanism; the document does not separate exclusion from PA. Concerta brand is E-flagged while generic methylphenidate ER (osm) is covered tier 2 QL, so the plan does not prefer the brand (boglActive false). Daytrana and Adhansia do not appear in this PDL text. Methylin (tier 4) is not separately assessed. Sig is standard FDA labeling, not the PDL. [Reused 2026-10-21 for uhc-md: same national UHC commercial PDL document as ny-uhc-commercial; Sonnet-checked in the NY pass. NY-specific "E" (may be excluded in NY) flags apply to NY plans; outside CT/NJ/NY the PDL legend (p.5) says E-flagged drugs may be excluded from coverage, so they are recorded as non-formulary here.] [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21)]
